//: The WEEKLY audit of the live site — .github/workflows/lighthouse.yml, job `production`. Separate from lighthouserc.json on purpose: that file budgets a locally-served production BUILD and asserts what the code should achieve in a lab; this one asserts what the deployed SITE must not fall below on a real network. The numbers used to be written twice — strictly in lighthouserc.json and loosely inline in the workflow — which is two sources of truth for one metric and the shape of defect this repository keeps shipping. The workflow now carries no thresholds and no URLs; they are all here.
//module-not-found: This file also exists because lhci auto-discovers lighthouserc.json from the working directory. The production job ran `lhci collect --url=...` from the repo root, so it picked up that file's `startServerCommand` and tried to boot a server from a dist/ directory that this job never builds: `Cannot find module .../dist/mastande-frontend/server/server.mjs`, MODULE_NOT_FOUND, run 10 on 19 October. Every weekly run since the domain started answering died there, before collecting anything. The job passes --config explicitly now, so the local-build settings cannot leak into a remote audit.

collect.//: www, not the apex. environment.prod.ts documents the apex as a 301 to www; auditing the apex measures the redirect hop and the LCP of whatever the old host serves while it is still in the chain.

settings.//: Same device as the budgets run, so a weekly number can be compared against a PR number. Desktop scores flatter and would hide exactly the regressions that matter to a South African audience on a phone.

assert.//aggregation: See lighthouserc.json: lhci's default "optimistic" aggregation reads the BEST of the three runs for a max assertion. This job's first ever completed run passed all four floors while its median run measured CLS 0.953 — nine times the bound it was asserting. Median, so the gate reads what a typical visitor gets.
//: Deliberately few. Each is a number this product has a real stake in, on the slow Android phone it is built for, and each is set at the level the site should not fall BELOW rather than at an aspiration — a weekly audit that fails on an aspiration gets muted.
categories:seo 0.9 — metadata, crawlability, tap targets. A drop here is almost always an accident.
largest-contentful-paint 4000ms — the board's hero and first room card. Google's 'poor' threshold is 4s; this fails only when a real person would call the page slow.
cumulative-layout-shift 0.1 — the 'good' bound. Layout shift on a listing card is how somebody taps the wrong room.

total-blocking-time 600ms — a PROXY for INP, which Lighthouse cannot measure in a lab run because it needs real interactions. Named as a proxy rather than reported as INP: they are not the same metric, and saying otherwise would be a claim this workflow cannot support.

MEASURED, once, on 21 October 2026 — run 11, the first audit this job has ever completed. Median run, mobile, simulated throttling: /pricing performance 0.98, CLS 0.017, LCP 1.1s; /how-it-works 0.97, CLS 0.05, LCP 1.1s; and the BOARD at / performance 0.62, LCP 3.3s, TBT 310ms, CLS 0.953. The board's CLS is nine times the bound asserted two lines above, and this run reported green because of the optimistic aggregation now fixed. That is the live site's number, not a lab guess, and docs/OUTSTANDING.md §87 carries it.
